status: S10 final: S9 merge plus the redo check (stages 1 to 3b), the orchestrator's decisions and the user's staged decisions of 26 Nov

quoted-evidence-rule.summary: Landscape deviations and departures from White Hound's conclusions or drawings are fine; nothing may directly contradict the quoted book evidence, and only such contradictions go to the user. Unbuilt map items are fine.
quoted-evidence-rule.words: I don't mind landscape deviations or conclusion deviations, as just nothing can directly contradict the quoted evidence ... That should be a principle going forward

unbuilt-map-items-fine.summary: Unbuilt White Hound map-key items (paddocks, the grandstand, the overflow exit, the boats) are a conclusion deviation only, resolved under the standing rule.

drive-dip.summary: No change to the drive's dip by the lake: 'the bottom of the drive' is its far end from the castle, and the gates come into view as one tops the cabin's terrace.

upper-hogsmeade-above-gates.summary: Upper Hogsmeade, 17.5-46 m above the gates, is accepted without earthworks: the walk up from the village to the gates holds from the High Street, and White Hound's own conclusion is not met by the upper fringe.

aragog-web-left-out.summary: Aragog's hollow is cut into dry Forest without his web; resolved by the orchestrator under the user's rule, and recorded as an omission.

gof-set-pieces-excluded.summary: The temporary Triwizard set pieces (paddocks, the Beauxbatons caravan, the swimming start and grandstands) are not modelled.

boats-excluded.summary: The first-years' boats are not modelled; the underground harbour's mouth is.

k2-sirius-cave.summary: Sirius's cave is not modelled: the tour's waypoint frames its place on the mountain, where it would be sub-pixel (limitation K2).

cliff-length-settled.summary: The cliff now runs round both of the castle's lake sides and its length is settled; the shore must still have lawns down to the water where the books need them.

one-nov-audit-fixes.summary: The 1 November audit's fixes stand: windows in all five changing rooms, the Hog's Head's bay windows and sign, the boarded Shack, Honeydukes' mullions, the streetlamps, and the night High Street dark but for streetlamps and lit upper windows.

astronomy-doors-keep.summary: The Astronomy Tower keeps its plan position beside the main doors rather than being stretched over them.

wh-conclusions-free.summary: White Hound's conclusions that rest on no passage of the seven novels or the three companion books (tiers 1-2 of canon-tiers) are accounted under the user's rule: the scene may follow or depart from them, and no row is needed. That covers etymology, architecture and outlooks he infers, and conclusions that rest only on Rowling's formal or informal statements, the films or other extras (tiers 3-5). Amended 26 Nov to follow canon-tiers.

canon-tiers.summary: Only two source tiers are binding canon, and their quotes must be met: (1) the seven novels and (2) the three companion books (QTtA, FB and BtB); the novels win where they conflict. Not binding, in White Hound's order: (3) Rowling's formal writing outside the books (e.g. the Famous Wizard cards); (4) her informal statements (interviews, chats, website comments); (5) the films and other extras. They may support a reading where canon is open but never stand against canon: a row may cite them only in a reading's basis (source:<page>:<line>) or in an alternative, never as its quote.
canon-tiers.words: wait, you should treat the companion books (two or three, right?) as canon too / We should keep this rule in its entirety if possible / Treat only the first two as fully canon

no-waivers.summary: The user answered the waiver question (D2) with option (c), no waivers: every row that does not hold stays open until the scene meets it, and no row carries a waiver.

reading-questions-26nov.summary: The user took the orchestrator's recommendation on each of the 11 reading-question and residual-split items (recs-v1.md section A): the readings the scene follows, the rows that do not hold, the unions of locators and the one conversion to an event.

alternatives.reading: The collision bend belongs to the station-road segment before the village lane separates.
alternatives.why: The proposed geometry refines the book claim but is not itself a binding requirement.
alternatives.result: The frozen row locates its hedged bend 467–483 m from the gates, beyond the 404 m fork. A different bend at 358 m has a hedge 4.3 m away, but all 15 tested pedestrian sightlines there were clear. The existence of that candidate does not relocate the collision witness. Orchestrator decision (redo check 1): D1; the row's chosen witness bend is not used (D2). The collision bend is where Harry, running for the school, comes round a bend into Hagrid without having seen him and ends up in the hedgerow. White Hound's own account relies on hedges or trees that hide the lane. The only bend before the fork, about 22-25 degrees at 322-358 m from the gates, has a field hedge about 1.5 m tall, far too low to hide Hagrid, and all 15 of seat A's pedestrian sightlines round it are clear. The shared station-road segment has no bend that could host the collision. Seat O's bend is real but doesn't meet the reading's own terms.
alternatives.result_other: A bend of about 22-25 degrees on 30-40 m chords lies 322-352 m from the gates, before the fork at 404-408 m, with a field hedge about 1.5 m tall 2.9 m from the centreline. My earlier bend test, 25 degrees on 15 m chords, missed it.

rows.assertion: The lane walked from the school's gates down to Hogsmeade twists, with several bends.

alternatives.reading: A winding lane to the village branches from the wider station road.

alternatives.result: The roads overlap for about 375 m, then diverge near 400–425 m. Seven comparable cross-sections farther along measure 7.0–8.5 m on the station arm and 4.0–5.25 m toward the village. The latter winds onward. A real, narrower village branch exists without assigning any particular barn.
alternatives.result_other: 404 m from the gates the station road, 6.5-7.0 m wide, turns off; the village lane, 4.5 m wide and bending 20-38 degrees at a time, runs on.

alternatives.reading: The village route bears gently right at a fork or continues straight while the station road branches away.
alternatives.why: The proposed geometry refines the book claim but is not itself a binding requirement.
alternatives.result: From the gates, the village route approaches the fork at 253 degrees and continues near 249–252 degrees. The station arm turns away toward 152 degrees. The traveller going to town therefore follows a nearly straight continuation, despite the large angle between the two outgoing roads.
alternatives.result_other: At the junction the village lane holds its line, changing 4 degrees, while the station road turns 93 degrees to the left.

alternatives.reading: Hogsmeade lies downslope and nearly a mile from the castle along the village connection.
alternatives.why: The proposed geometry refines the book claim but is not itself a binding requirement.
alternatives.result: From the castle doors through the gates and along the lane, the first village houses are 1,640 m away, just over a mile, and the High Street's end 1,746 m; they lie 7 and 14 m below the doors, the inns 18-20 m below. The lane itself rises 32 m and falls 30 m on the way. Orchestrator decision (redo check 2): D1. The reading's words are approximate. Both seats find the village below the castle: seat A has the High Street turn 13.1 m lower; seat O has houses 7 to 14 m lower and the inns 18 to 20 m. The nearest houses come 1,640 m along the way (seat O), and footprints within 50 m of the road begin at 1,769 m (seat A): 1.0 to 1.1 miles. At the precision 'nearly a mile' carries, a village that begins there is consistent with it. Seat A dissents: measured to the High Street turn, 1,945 m or 1.21 miles, the mileage does not fit.
alternatives.result_other: From the castle steps via the gate to the school-road turn on High Street is 1,945 m, descending 13.1 m: 1.21 miles. The first village footprint within 20 m of the road comes at 1,927 m. Even a 50 m margin starts at 1,769 m, still above the starting elevation. The descent fits; the proposed mileage does not.

alternatives.result: A broad central block covers about 3,034 square metres. Distinct masses of about 569 and 1,209 square metres flank it to west and east respectively. Their roof centroids have eastings near −110, −43 and +83 m in west-to-east order; the castle also has other ranges.

alternatives.reading: The west wing is no cross-bar capping the western end of an east-west main range.
alternatives.why: The proposed geometry refines the book claim but is not itself a binding requirement.
alternatives.result: He rejects a crossing bar at the western end of an east-west main block, since it would shade the doors from the sunset. Both seats answered #a3 and #a7 false; the plan's axis runs 168 degrees. The west range meets the short east-west link only at its own south end, running north, and sunset reaches the doors. Orchestrator decision (redo check 1): D1, with the words read in their source sense. The reading condenses White Hound's rejection of a cross-bar that caps the west end of an east-west main building and would cut the evening sun off from the main doors. His adopted layout keeps wings at right angles at the ends, along the sides, and the row's #a7 wording draws the same line between the ends and the entrance face. In the scene the entrance block runs at 71.5 degrees with its doors facing about 253 degrees. The western block leaves near that end through a 15.9 m link and runs north along the side, and both seats find evening light reaching the doors. Read literally, as seat A did, #a2 would reject White Hound's own layout. The reading is reworded below to restore the qualifier.
alternatives.result_other: The whole roof envelope trends 171 degrees. Within it, the main block's long axis is 71.5 degrees and the labelled western block's is 161.6. A 15.9 m link joins them 7% along the main block from its west end. At block scale the rejected perpendicular arrangement is present.

alternatives.reading: An east-west main range has an angled front facing southwest.

alternatives.result_other: The castle's long axis runs north-south (168 degrees), 366 by 212 m; the entrance front faces 253.5, but no east-west main range exists.

alternatives.reading: The Owlery's block lies beside the branch into the west wing rather than within that wing.

alternatives.result: West Tower's centre is 4.4 m outside the central roof and 23.5 m outside the western block. A distinct 15.9 m connecting range comes within 10.6 m of the tower and meets both blocks. The Owlery therefore lies beside the junction, not inside the wing footprint.
alternatives.result_other: West Tower stands where the east-west link near z 0 meets the west range's south end: at the branch, not out along the wing.

alternatives.reading: Returning from the Owlery bypasses a side turning into the west wing.
alternatives.why: The proposed geometry refines the book claim but is not itself a binding requirement.
alternatives.result: Measured eastward along the main range, the Owlery drum meets it near 5.2 m. The roofed west-wing branch joins at 5.3–10.9 m; the main roof continues to 115.5 m. An eastbound return thus passes the separate branch in plan. This establishes the layout, not the positions of indoor doors.
alternatives.result_other: Both seats answered #a4 true: West Tower stands where the east-west link meets the west range's south end. Heading back east along that link, the turn north into the west range opens at the tower's corner and is passed by. The massing carries the route; no corridors are modelled anywhere.

alternatives.reading: The west wing points away from the main block, while the eastern wing may be parallel or reflexed.
alternatives.why: The proposed geometry refines the book claim but is not itself a binding requirement.
alternatives.result: The labelled western block projects 41 m outward at 347 degrees. The eastern projection runs 65 m at 143 degrees; their long roof axes differ by 8.5 degrees. The evening beam reaches the entrance. Middle water is visible from a lawn flank, not from any of 63 tested central grass eyes. Orchestrator decision (redo check 1): D1. In White Hound's model the main block is the east-west building that carries the main doors; in the scene that is the entrance block (axis 71.5 degrees, doors facing about 253). The western block springs from near its west end and projects about 41 m outward at 347 degrees, so it points away from that block, not back across it. The reading's 'may' leaves the east wing's form open. Seat O measured against the north-south middle band, which isn't the block with the doors. The mapping is the same as for #a2.
alternatives.result_other: By pointing away he means a wing running out from the main body, set against one folded back parallel to it. The named west range is a 150 m bar at 3 degrees, within 4 of the middle band it flanks (the central block of #a1): it lies parallel, the reflexed form he allows only for the east wing.

rows.note: Book checks decide holds. Optional interpretations are unmeasured and assessed separately; no scene fixes are authorized. Orchestrator decision (S9): D3 by analogy: the camera cannot go below the surface, so the depicted property is the water's murk. Its extinction of 0.8 per metre leaves 5% contrast at about 3.7 m, close to the stated ten feet. Seat A dissents: no submerged view is modelled, and the shader applies the murk along vertical depth only. A future underwater view would need the murk along the sight line to keep holding.
facts: Both attempted underwater eyes stopped 1.50 m above water. The shader weights the bed by exp(−0.8 × vertical depth), leaving 5% at 3.74 m.
Water of constant depth gives the same bed weight regardless of a swimmer's horizontal viewing distance. The model supplies no submerged visibility measurement.
Extinction of 0.8 per metre halves contrast every 0.87 m of water, whichever way the light travels.
The camera cannot go below the surface, so the coefficient is the only measure of underwater sight.

Seat A's rewrite would require the window to be shown open. The book states no such lasting condition, and a rewrite must not add a requirement the passage lacks, as G's new-requirement rule has it. Orchestrator decision (redo check 2): Confirms the rc1 decision. D3 and static-exteriors (no new animations).
